summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Hirofumi Toda studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University (attested 1985–1999) and was a special researcher at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, Hiroko Kawanami studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. Her career includes serving as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).
A scholar of Indology and philosophy, Hiroko Matsuoka was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held a post at Leipzig University (attested 2016).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Hiromasa Tosaki earned a PhD from Kyushu University and studied at Harvard. He studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Satkari Mookerjee, and others, later serving as professor at Kyushu University (~1976–1994).
Hiromi Habata is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D from the University of Freiburg. She held a research post at the University of Munich (attested 2014).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Hiromi Yoshimura held appointments at Ryukoku University, including as a full-time lecturer (attested 1987) and in a later post attested in 2006.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Hiromu Kitanishi studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor from around 1967 to 1995.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Hironori Tanaka studied as a PhD student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020) and also held a post there.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Hiroo Kashiwagi completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He served as a professor at Matsusaka University (attested 1982) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College.

A specialist in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Hiroo Sato studied at Tohoku University (~1972–1981). He later worked at Morioka College (~1987–1994) and served as a professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi is a linguist who studied at International Christian University (~1980–1986) and earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (~1991–1998). He became a professor at Nanzan University around 2005.

A scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, Hiroshi Araki completed his degrees, including a PhD, at Kyoto University. He taught at Osaka University and served as a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).
Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1948 to 1953 and later held a post at Hokkaido University.

A Buddhist studies and sinology scholar, Hiroshi Kanno studied at the University of Tokyo. He has served at The Institute of Oriental Philosophy, as director at Soka University, and as director of the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2002–2009).

An Indology and philosophy scholar, Hiroshi Kuroda completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1970–1976). He served as an assistant professor at Osaka Gakuin University (~1983–1987) and Osaka Gakuin Junior College (~1987).

An Indology and philosophy scholar, Hiroshi Marui earned degrees, including a doctorate, from the University of Tokyo and studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and served as associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1999–2018).
Specializing in Indology, Hiroshi Maruyama served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 1987) and headed the Ayurveda Research Society (attested 1987).
Hiroshi Nemoto, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, completed an MA at Hiroshima University and later served as a professor there (attested 2015).
Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He held a post as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).
A linguist, Hisanosuke Izui studied at Kyoto University from around 1925 to 1928. He later held an academic post at Kyoto Sangyo University from around 1969 to 1978.
